reason: Hypothesis A proposes a physically sound transient liquid-phase sintering mechanism with B4C that forms a crystalline intergranular ZrB12 barrier, directly addressing oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion within the specified lower-temperature constraint (1700–1800°C), and its falsification experiment is specific and decisive. Hypothesis B relies on an amorphous silicate layer from Si doping, which is less stable and protective in the high-temperature (>1200°C) and liquid-metal environments described, and its sintering mechanism below 1700°C is less well-grounded for ZrB2.
